title: Storytelling

script.script:
My dad's sidepiece showed up to my parents' fortieth anniversary party.

She didn't know we all knew.

She was 64 wearing a dress that my 38 year old sister couldn't pull off.

My mom saw her walking in and didn't flinch.

Because by then my mom looked better.

Let me tell you how.

My parents have been married for forty years.

It hasn't been perfect.

My daddy had an affair about eight years ago with a woman named Lorraine from his lodge.

It lasted two years.

My mama found out.

They went through it.

They stayed together.

That's how my parents' generation handles things.

You don't leave.

You deal with it.

They dealt with it.

But here's what my mama never dealt with.

Lorraine is 64 years old and looks like God personally carved her.

Her skin is smooth.

Her body is tight.

She moves like a woman who knows every man in the room is looking and doesn't care.

My mama is 62 and has been fighting her body since menopause hit.

She tried every diet.

Every pill.

Every program.

She lost the same 20 pounds 15 times and gained it back every single time.

And every time she saw Lorraine at a church function or at the grocery store or at somebody's funeral, she'd come home and not eat for two days.

Not because she was dieting.

Because seeing Lorraine made her sick.

About two years after the affair ended, my mama had a breakdown.

Not about my daddy.

About her body.

She sat at the kitchen table one night and said I can't do this anymore.

I can't keep looking like this while that woman looks like that.

I can't keep being the wife he stayed with while she's the woman he wanted.

I need to change something or I'm gonna lose my mind.

My aunt Patricia, mama's older sister, had been waiting for this moment.

She'd been watching mama spiral for two years and hadn't said anything because mama wasn't ready.

That night she was ready.

Aunt Patricia sat down across from her and put a soft cotton pack and a dark glass bottle on the table.

She said I've been using this for eleven years and I've been waiting for you to ask me for help.

She said that weight you're carrying is not from food.

It's waste.

She said your body has a drainage system and it shut down years ago.

Everything you eat is fine.

Your body just stopped taking out the garbage and it's been building up inside you.

Pooling in your belly.

Your thighs.

Your face.

Your arms.

She said this is what Egyptian women have used for three thousand years to drain the sludge that menopause leaves behind.

She said the ricinoleic acid in castor oil absorbs through your skin three and a half inches deep into the tissue where the drainage channels are clogged.

Calms the inflammation keeping the channels shut.

Softens the hardened waste.

The compression holds it against your drainage center all night.

The warmth widens the channels so the sludge moves through.

Pills get destroyed by stomach acid.

This pack is direct delivery while you sleep.

She said wrap this around your belly every night before bed.

That's it.

That's what I do.

That's what every woman my age who isn't starving herself does.

The brand is called Haven & Spool.

90% ricinoleic acid.

USDA organic.

Organic cotton that feels like a warm hug.

Nothing to swallow.

Mama took it home.

Started that night.

First week the bathroom became her best friend.

Things moving.

Shifting.

Flushing.

By day four she called Aunt Patricia and said Trish something's happening.

Week two the puffiness in her face she'd carried for a decade just left.

My sister saw her and said mama did you get filler?

She said girl no I'm draining.

Week three her belly started going down.

Same food.

Same everything.

She put on a dress from the back of her closet and it zipped.

She called me crying.

Happy crying.

Week four down 15 pounds.

By month two down 28.

By month four she lost 42 pounds and looked like a completely different woman.

Not skinny.

Vibrant.

Her skin was glowing.

Her energy was back.

She was moving different.

Talking different.

Standing different.

My daddy looked at her like he was falling in love all over again with someone he'd been sleeping next to for thirty eight years.

When the anniversary party happened we threw them a party at the church hall.

Family.

Friends.

The whole congregation.

Mama wore a gold dress my sister picked out for her.

She looked stunning.

Everyone in the room was staring at her.

She was 62 and she looked better than she did in her wedding photos.

Then Lorraine walked in.

She didn't know we all knew who she was.

She'd been invited by someone from the lodge who didn't know the history.

She walked in wearing a fitted black dress looking the way she always looks.

64.

Beautiful.

Confident.

Like she owned the room just by being in it.

And for the first time in eight years my mama didn't flinch.

She didn't go to the bathroom to cry.

She didn't stop breathing.

She looked at Lorraine across the room and she didn't feel anything except calm.

Because for the first time she wasn't comparing from a place of losing.

She looked down at her own body in that gold dress and she knew.

She didn't just match Lorraine.

She passed her.

Lorraine saw my mama from across the room and did a double take so obvious three people noticed.

She looked at her from head to toe.

Something shifted in her face.

She looked confused.

Like she was seeing someone she didn't recognize standing next to the man she used to sleep with.

My mama walked up to her.

Smiled.

Said thank you for coming.

And walked away.

There was no confrontation.

No drama.

No revenge speech.

Just a woman in a gold dress who finally won a war she'd been losing for eight years.

Not because she fought harder.

Because she finally found out what Lorraine knew all along.

The weight was never about food.

It was drainage.

And once you drain it, everything changes.
